title: Cohomology tail bounds from a regular hyperplane restriction
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$, $X=\mathbf P^n_k$, and $E$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Use twists $E(d)=E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. Let $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ be a nonzero linear form, and let $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow X$ be its hyperplane closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Fix an identification $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ carrying $i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$ to $\mathcal O_H(d)$ for every integer $d$. Put $G=i^*E$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and assume $G$ is coherent and multiplication by $s$ is injective on $E(d-1)\to E(d)$ for every integer $d$. Let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and assume $G$ is $m$-regular, that is,
$$H^q(H,G(m-q))=0\qquad(1\leq q\leq n-1).$$
Put $h=\dim_k H^1(X,E(m))$, the finite vector-space dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Then
$$H^q(X,E(t))=0\qquad(q\geq2,\ t\geq m),$$
and
$$H^1(X,E(t))=0\qquad(t\geq m+h).$$

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, proof: paragraphs beginning Let i >= 2, We still have to control H1, and Suppose d > m prime. Extracted for an arbitrary coherent module with regular hyperplane restriction; the conclusions are cohomology thresholds, not the erroneous closing regularity estimate.

proof.text: Every $E(d)$ is coherent: on an open trivializing $\mathcal O_X(d)$ it is isomorphic to $E$, and the finite-type and kernel conditions defining coherence are local. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Applying [lem-pc-projective-space-coherent-finiteness] to $E(d)$ therefore makes every $H^q(X,E(d))$ finite-dimensional. In particular $h$ is a nonnegative integer. By [lem-sfb-fixed-hyperplane-restriction-cohomology], write $a_d^q:H^q(X,E(d-1))\to H^q(X,E(d))$ for multiplication by $s$, and $r_d:H^0(X,E(d))\to H^0(H,G(d))$ for restriction. We have the stated long exact sequence, surjectivity of restriction on linear forms, and $r_{d+1}(uv)=r_d(u)(v|_H)$. The fixed-section lemma applies to the very $s$ of the hypothesis and does not require $k$ infinite. Choose the twist comparisons on $H$ compatibly with products: from a degree-one comparison sending a local frame $a$ to $cb$, send $a^d$ to $c^d b^d$ for every integer $d$, with negative powers interpreted using dual frames. The twist transition rule makes these formulas glue. The identity $c^dc^e=c^{d+e}$ proves compatibility with multiplication. Thus the product on the restricted twists in the fixed-section lemma is identified with the standard product used by the regularity consequence in step 2.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, middle cohomology paragraphs, applied to E and its given hyperplane restriction G.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-m-regular-coherent-sheaf-consequences] on $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ to the coherent module $G$, with regularity parameter $m$. It gives $H^j(H,G(d))=0$ for every $j>0$ and $d\geq m$, including $n=1$ where $H\cong\mathbf P^0_k$. For every $d\geq m$, multiplication $H^0(H,G(d))\otimes_k H^0(H,\mathcal O_H(1))\to H^0(H,G(d+1))$ is surjective. Apply [lem-pc-projective-space-serre-vanishing] to $E$ over the Noetherian field $k$: choose $D\geq0$ such that $H^q(X,E(t))=0$ for all $q>0$ and all $t\geq D$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, middle cohomology paragraphs, applied to E and its given hyperplane restriction G.

proof.text: Fix $q\geq2$ and $t\geq m$. For each $d\geq m$, the segment $H^{q-1}(H,G(d))\to H^q(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{a_d^q}H^q(X,E(d))$ is exact and its left term is zero, so $a_d^q$ is injective. Choose the integer $T=\max(t,D)$. If $T=t$, Serre vanishing already gives $H^q(X,E(t))=0$. Otherwise each index $d=t+1,\ldots,T$ satisfies $d\geq m$, so the composite of these finitely many injections embeds $H^q(X,E(t))$ into the zero space $H^q(X,E(T))$. Hence $H^q(X,E(t))=0$. The same argument applies separately to every $q\geq2$, proving the whole higher-cohomology assertion.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, middle cohomology paragraphs, applied to E and its given hyperplane restriction G.

proof.text: For $d\geq m$, exactness of $H^1(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{a_d^1}H^1(X,E(d))\to H^1(H,G(d))=0$ makes $a_d^1$ surjective. Denote the preceding connecting map by $\delta_d:H^0(H,G(d))\to H^1(X,E(d-1))$. Exactness gives $\ker a_d^1=\operatorname{im}\delta_d$ and $\ker\delta_d=\operatorname{im}r_d$. Consequently $a_d^1$ is injective precisely when $\operatorname{im}\delta_d=0$, precisely when $\delta_d=0$, precisely when $\ker\delta_d=H^0(H,G(d))$, and hence precisely when $r_d$ is surjective. This identifies the actual maps used in the propagation step.

proof.text:
Suppose $d\geq m+1$ and $a_d^1$ is injective. Step 4 makes $r_d$ surjective. For any $w\in H^0(H,G(d+1))$, the multiplication surjection of step 2 writes $w=\sum_{
u=1}^N g_
u\ell_
u$, with $g_
u\in H^0(H,G(d))$ and $\ell_
u\in H^0(H,\mathcal O_H(1))$. Lift $g_
u$ to $u_
u\in H^0(X,E(d))$ using $r_d$, and lift $\ell_
u$ to $v_
u\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ using the linear-form restriction surjection from [lem-sfb-fixed-hyperplane-restriction-cohomology]. Then $r_{d+1}(\sum u_
u v_
u)=\sum g_
u\ell_
u=w$. Thus $r_{d+1}$ is surjective, so $a_{d+1}^1$ is injective by step 4. This is the induction step: starting from the assumed injectivity at $d$, induction on $e-d\geq0$ gives injectivity at every $e\geq d$. Set $T=\max(d,D)$. For $e=d,\ldots,T$ the maps $a_e^1$ are injective; their finite composite embeds $H^1(X,E(d-1))$ into $H^1(X,E(T))=0$ by Serre vanishing. Hence $H^1(X,E(d-1))=0$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, middle cohomology paragraphs, applied to E and its given hyperplane restriction G.

proof.text: Put $V_t=H^1(X,E(t))$ and $b_t=\dim_k V_t$ for $t\geq m$. The maps $V_t\to V_{t+1}$ are surjective. If $V_t\ne0$, step 5 with $d=t+1\geq m+1$ shows that this map cannot be injective. Choose $0\ne z$ in its kernel and extend $z$ to a basis of the finite-dimensional $V_t$. Images of the remaining $b_t-1$ basis vectors span the quotient $V_{t+1}$, so $b_{t+1}\leq b_t-1$. If $V_t=0$, its surjective image $V_{t+1}$ is zero. We prove $b_{m+r}\leq\max(h-r,0)$ by induction on the nonnegative integer $r$. At $r=0$ this is $b_m=h$. If $b_{m+r}=0$, surjectivity gives $b_{m+r+1}=0$. Otherwise the induction hypothesis forces $h-r>0$, and the strict decrease gives $b_{m+r+1}\leq b_{m+r}-1\leq h-r-1=\max(h-(r+1),0)$. This proves the induction step in both cases. In particular $b_{m+h}=0$, and all $V_t$ for $t\geq m+h$ are zero. This proves the first-cohomology assertion, including $h=0$.
